title: El Cortez Hotel-Casino
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Siegel group ownership of El Cortez 1945-46
quote: By 1945, mobster Bugsy Siegel had taken over the property.
summary: Encyclopedia entry: Siegel took over El Cortez by 1945 and sold it in 1946 to fund the Flamingo; later owners Houssels/Moore group (1946-63), then Jackie Gaughan from 1963. It hedges on who the real partners were.
limits: Not a court or gaming-board record; ownership by Siegel's group is stated, but no finding is cited. Contradicts the current 'no documented mob ownership' summary.

title: El Cortez (Las Vegas)
ask_addressed: dates: opening 1941, ownership chain, Siegel purchase 1945 and buy-back 1946
quote: Houssels purchased the hotel back from Siegel's group in 1946 for $766,000.
summary: Gives opening 7 Nov 1941 (Hicks and Grayson), 1945 sale to Siegel, Lansky, Greenbaum, Sedway, 1946 buy-back by Houssels, Gaughan 1963, sale to Kenny Epstein 2008. Cites FBI file material about a Minneapolis figure linked to Siegel at El Cortez.
limits: Wikipedia, context only. It dates Gaughan's sale to 2008; Online Nevada says a 2002 sale to Barrick Gaming was announced; the two are not reconciled. Venue still open.

title: Guy McAfee
ask_addressed: dates: Golden Nugget opening 1946 and founding partners
quote: In 1946, McAfee opened the Golden Nugget with a décor based on the nineteenth-century Barbary Coast era in San Francisco.
summary: Confirms 1946 opening under Guy McAfee (casino planned from 1945 as the Golden Nugget Saloon at 125 Fremont); partners Jake Kozloff and Beldon Katelman by 1951.
limits: Author and date shown only as 'Last Updated July 30, 2015'. Says nothing on later owners.

title: Guy McAfee
quote: McAfee denied any involvement and was never charged.
summary: McAfee was a former Los Angeles vice squad captain who ran illegal casinos in California; the governor objected to his reputation but the district attorney said Nevada law gave no ground to refuse. Nothing here ties the Nugget to a crime syndicate.
limits: That is about a 1931 Los Angeles murder matter, not the Nugget. Shows a reputation for vice, not a documented organised-crime tie.

title: Golden Nugget Las Vegas
ask_addressed: lineage: later owners of Golden Nugget
quote: The Golden Nugget was sold in 2003, for $215 million to Poster Financial Group, owned by Timothy Poster and Thomas Breitling.
summary: Chain: Wynn majority shareholder 1973; sold to MGM Grand, Inc. with Mirage Resorts in 2000; Poster Financial 2003; Landry's closed 27 Sept 2005.
limits: Wikipedia, context only. No organised-crime content.

title: Estes Kefauver (1903-1963) / The Kefauver hearings in Las Vegas
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Kefauver Committee 1950-51 and Las Vegas
quote: The Kefauver Committee's final report was more than 11,000 pages long, out of which only four pages pertained to Las Vegas.
summary: The Las Vegas hearing was brief; the page does not name the Golden Nugget or El Cortez as findings. It shows that the Kefauver record is thin for these venues.
limits: Does not mention these venues in the text read. Not a primary hearing transcript.

title: Four Queens and Fremont
quote: the Fremont became part of the Argent Corporation, which turned out to be a front for organized crime families in Chicago, Kansas City, and Milwaukee.
summary: Says Gaming Control Board and Gaming Commission forced out Glick and the next owners (Sachs and Tobman), the state asked Boyd Gaming to run it, and Boyd later bought it. Also gives 1956 opening, builder Eddie Levinson, investor Lou Lurie.
limits: Encyclopedia summary, not the board's own finding. Does not mention a conviction.

title: State Fines Argent Corp.; Revokes Game License
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Nevada Gaming Commission action against the Fremont Hotel licence
quote: Gaming licenses for controversial Argent Corp. were revoked Thursday during a Nevada Gaming Commission meeting
summary: Contemporary report of the Commission revoking (held in abeyance to 31 Dec 1980) licences of Argent, Glick, the Fremont Hotel and others, with $500,000 in fines, over about $7 million embezzled from four casinos in 1974-76.
limits: A news report of the Commission's action, not the Commission's order. It speaks of embezzlement and weak controls; it does not itself name organised-crime families.

title: Central States, Southeast, Southwest Areas Pension Fund
ask_addressed: lineage: Teamsters pension loan to Fremont 1961 and Dalitz
quote: The fund soon backed loans to Dalitz for hotel-casinos he controlled: the Stardust ($6 million) in 1960 and Fremont ($4 million) in 1961.
summary: Shows a Teamsters pension loan to the Fremont in 1961 for a casino the entry says Moe Dalitz controlled, and calls the fund 'the mob's bank'. It is a thread to check against the 1956 owner list.
limits: Conflicts with the Levinson/Lurie 1956 ownership given elsewhere; the relationship is not explained. No court record cited.

title: Argent Corporation
ask_addressed: mob-tie: skim at Argent casinos and 1983 indictment
quote: federal, state and local gaming officials in Nevada confirmed that these casinos were controlled by organized crime families in the Midwest
summary: Argent (Allen Glick) bought Recrion, owner of the Stardust and Fremont, in 1974 with a Teamsters loan; skimming of $7-15 million; a 1983 federal case indicted 15 people. Glick was never charged.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; does not give the outcome of the case. The record's 'brought convictions' claim was not checked against a court page.

title: Fremont Hotel and Casino
ask_addressed: dates: Fremont opening 1956 and ownership chain
quote: In 1974, Allen Glick's Argent Corporation purchased the Fremont and in 1976 expanded the casino at a cost of $4 million.
summary: Opened 18 May 1956, owned by Ed Levinson and Lou Lurie; Argent 1974; Sam and Bill Boyd bought it in 1983 (Boyd Gaming); still open.

title: Railroad Pass Casino
ask_addressed: dates: Railroad Pass opening 1931 and ownership chain
summary: Opened 1 Aug 1931 as Railroad Pass Club (licence no. 4 under its latest name); Verchota 1975; Gold Strike Resorts 1985; Circus Circus 1995; MGM Mirage 2005; Joseph DeSimone 2015. No organised-crime content.
limits: Wikipedia, context only. Does not support the 'no allegations in regulatory records' wording: no regulatory record was opened.

title: Carson Nugget
ask_addressed: dates: Carson Nugget opening 1954 and ownership chain
quote: Richard Graves opened the casino, known then as the Carson City Nugget, on March 1, 1954.
summary: Graves 1954; Pogue and Armstrong Sept 1956; six Nevada-licensed buyers (incl. three Adams brothers) Dec 1958; Dean DiLullo/M1 Gaming 2015. No organised-crime content.
limits: Wikipedia, context only. Owners between 1958 and 2015 are missing. The 'family-owned throughout' claim is not supported by this chain.

title: Don Laughlin, architect behind Southern Nevada town, dead at 92
ask_addressed: dates: Riverside Resort opening 1966 and founder
summary: Obituary: Don Laughlin bought a boarded-up motel on the riverfront and opened the Riverside Resort in 1966; he remained its owner until his death in 2023. No organised-crime allegations appear.
limits: Obituary, not a regulatory record. Absence of allegations here is weak evidence.

title: Riverside Resort Hotel & Casino
quote: He opened the Riverside Resort on August 2, 1966.
summary: Gives the exact opening date and expansions (1972, 1975, 1983, 1986, 1994).

title: Colorado Belle
ask_addressed: dates: Colorado Belle opening 1987 and closure 2020
quote: Plans for Colorado Belle were unveiled in 1985 and it opened on July 1, 1987, at a cost of $80 million.
summary: Opened 1 July 1987 (Circus Circus; Mandalay 1999; MGM Mirage 2005); Marnell/Sher 2007; Golden Entertainment 2019; closed 17 Mar 2020 and kept closed indefinitely.
limits: Wikipedia, context only. Its history section opens with a 1979-84 casino whose link to the Colorado Belle site is unclear. The page says it remains closed.

title: Edgewater Hotel and Casino
ask_addressed: mob-tie: neighbouring Laughlin property, licensing concern
quote: raised concerns about alleged connections between some partners in the ownership group and members of the Detroit crime family
summary: Concerns the Edgewater (opened 1981), next door and later under the same owners; not the Colorado Belle. Shows the board did screen early Laughlin owners.
limits: About a different property and a licensing concern only. Not evidence about the Colorado Belle.
